Risk officer assessment: I recommend refusing. This coin is down 84% from its 30-minute high and 76% over 30 minutes, with net outflow in the last 15 minutes (sells 28.5 SOL vs buys 20.2 SOL) and 119 sellers against 65 buyers. The 33.7 SOL pool is thin, so a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs plus a 30-second execution delay would be heavily impacted, and a stop-loss could fill far below its trigger.

The base rate for random buys in this window is roughly -20%, and this coin is already in a steep downtrend, so momentum is against us. The "Super Gooner Intelligence" name and "agent-net.fun" metadata host are unverified and not a reason to buy.

If the desk overrides, the most I'd support is a $5 ticket, a 20% stop, and a 15-minute hold, but only after the price stabilizes and sell pressure visibly fades. Any size should be refused if sell flow continues to exceed buy flow, the pool shrinks further, or the price breaks below the current level.
memos.scout:
The case for buying SGI now is weak, and the brief mostly argues against it.

The strongest points are these: the curve shows broad participation (667 buyers, top-3 share 9.2%, bundle share 7.4%, no airdrop dump), and the first two minutes after graduation saw 130.8 SOL from 350 non-agent buyers with a sell-to-buy ratio near 1.0. That suggests the launch was not obviously manufactured.

But that demand is gone. In the last 15 minutes, buys were 20.2 SOL against 28.5 SOL of sells, net outflow of 8.3 SOL, with sellers (119) outnumbering buyers (65). The coin is down 76% over 30 minutes and sits 84% below its 30-minute high. Liquidity is only 33.7 SOL, so a $20 ticket faces meaningful impact and fees of 1.4-5.1%, and a 30-second execution lag in a falling market.

I can't name a reason demand will return in 30-60 minutes. Recent sellers are outpacing buyers, and the base rate for random buys of coins in this state is negative. Recommendation: skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is continued distribution into a thin pool. SGI is down 83.9% from its 30-minute high and 76% over 30 minutes, with the last 15 minutes showing net outflow of 8.29 SOL (sells 28.49 vs buys 20.2) and 119 sellers against 65 buyers. Sell-to-buy in the first two minutes after graduation was 1.04, so early buyers have been exiting, not holding. Pool depth is only 33.7 SOL, so a $20 round trip with 1.4-5.1% costs plus impact is a real drag, and a 5% bounce barely clears fees. The "organic" label rests on a 7.4% bundle share and a launch bot present at launch, which doesn't rule out ongoing sell pressure. A coin falling this hard with more sellers than buyers is a falling knife with thin liquidity. Skip.
